findings.summary: The verifier does not enforce the standard-library-only constraint and therefore accepts behaviorally correct submissions built on vendored or installed third-party Python code.
findings.rationale: Proven by execution: a candidate whose ed.py only execs a GNU ed binary staged beside it passed the returned verifier with reward 1. Every graded run now goes through a launcher that ends the run when the program starts a process, loads native code or imports from outside the standard library and its own files, the launcher is checked against four probe programs, and a separate test reads the delivered package for binaries and foreign imports. The same launcher candidate now scores 0.

findings.summary: The visible corpus never checks that options after FILE are rejected rather than accepted in arbitrary argv order.
findings.rationale: The invocation grammar says each option is its own argument before the optional FILE, so the forms the finding names do not occur. GNU ed 1.19 itself accepts them as well: -Es, -pfoo and -G all run, and an option written after FILE takes effect, so a rejection is not the required behaviour and grading one would fail the authority.

contract_citation.anchor: Each comes as its own argument before the optional FILE
